summary: A BARE entry with an explicit default port was stripped scheme-agnostically, so one declared origin trusted a second undeclared one -- the same defect class the commit exists to close, on the axis it did not test
classification_rationale: The commit's own test SECTION('a bare entry stays scheme-agnostic, and that is deliberate') pinned the defect as intended, and the changelog claimed a guarantee ('only when it is the default for that entry's own scheme') that was false for every bare entry. Fixed by refusing the ambiguous shape rather than guessing a scheme; test and changelog corrected.

trigger: `--csrf-trusted-origin null:443` -- the `null` guard ran BEFORE the port strip, so the canonical form became bare `null`
summary: Both the `null` and the empty-entry guards inspected the intermediate value rather than the canonical one, so a port suffix smuggled past each
classification_rationale: cpp-expert derived HIGH (I1, defeats the control this commit added); security-guardian derived MEDIUM (I6), explicitly considering and rejecting the false-assurance raise because the published sentence stays true for the token itself. MEDIUM upheld: reaching it needs an operator to type nonsense config, and the human reviewer graded the entire `null` issue a nice-to-have. security-guardian additionally found the SINK -- the same ordering defect affects the empty guard -- which cpp-expert did not.
adjudicated_by: orchestrator (read both derivations; security-guardian's I6 upheld over cpp-expert's I1)

trigger: `--csrf-trusted-origin https://null` for a real internal host named `null`
summary: The `null` refusal was not gated on a bare entry, so a scheme-qualified real hostname was silently dropped -- a new FALSE REFUSAL introduced by the guard
classification_rationale: RFC 6454's opaque serialisation is the bare token only. The commit's own comment implied otherwise. Now gated on `scheme.empty()`.

trigger: `--csrf-trusted-origin null` (or any all-invalid config) at boot
summary: Boot output for an all-rejected config was byte-identical to the flag being unset, so the operator's first symptom was the opaque 403 the logging exists to diagnose
classification_rationale: E0 -- fires unconditionally on the boot path, no actor required. Now warns with accepted-versus-supplied counts and names the rejected shapes.

summary: The same loose empty-scheme branch under-matched in the other direction: entry normalised to `h` while the request canonicalised to `h:80`, refusing an origin that matched before the commit
classification_rationale: Same root cause as G1-01 and closed by the same fix -- the ambiguous shape is now refused at normalisation with a boot warning, instead of being silently mangled into something unmatchable.
caused_by: a83f88d0 (the scheme-aware strip introduced the asymmetry)

trigger: A maintainer reads the hover/Doxygen for either function
summary: The new helper was inserted between `normalise_trusted_origins`'s doc block and the function, so 28 lines including the load-bearing #1271 CLI11 warning documented the wrong function and the right one had none
classification_rationale: Reported independently by cpp-expert, docs-writer, cpp-safety and security-guardian -- the strongest class in this run. Helper and its own comment moved above the block.

trigger: A refactor follows the documented normalisation sequence
summary: The stated normalisation ORDER did not match the code, and the documented order was the WEAKER one -- following it would have re-admitted `NULL` and `null/x` as entries
classification_rationale: Replaced with the actual seven-step order, and the reason steps 6 and 7 must not swap is stated inline.

trigger: `origin_is_same_site(host, "https://", "", {""})` -- an empty `want` matched a degenerate entry
summary: The matcher's safety rested on an invariant enforced only in a different function; it now refuses an empty or host-less `want` itself
classification_rationale: E6 today -- normalisation drops every such entry and all five call sites take the normalised span -- so LOW by derivation. Folded anyway because defence in depth at the chokepoint is cheaper than the coupling.

summary: Userinfo was rejected on the request side but kept at normalisation, so the boot log advertised an entry that could never match -- dishonest deployment evidence
classification_rationale: Fail-closed, so no admission risk; the defect is in the evidence, which is what the boot log exists to be.

trigger: A regression makes normalisation drop an entry a test then indexes
summary: Seven new assertions indexed `[0]` on an unchecked temporary, so a regression would be out-of-range UB rather than a clean failure -- sharper here because adjacent sections deliberately assert `.empty()`
classification_rationale: All sites now bind a named `const auto` and `REQUIRE` the size first, matching the file's own convention two sections up.

trigger: A reader parses the `is_default` ternary's precedence from its indentation
summary: The ternary was correct but its clang-format continuation indent misled about `||` binding
classification_rationale: Resolved incidentally -- deleting the loose empty-scheme branch removed the ternary entirely.

trigger: One `std::string` copy per gated POST at the allowlist entry point
summary: `*extracted` is dead after the call, so the copy was free to elide
classification_rationale: Not a performance finding -- cpp-safety was explicit that the brief's 'copy per allowlist entry' does not occur, since the call is outside the loop. Taken because it is one word.

trigger: A future edit changes one copy of the SameSite correction and not the other
summary: The ~10-line SameSite threat-model correction now exists verbatim in two files and will drift; the durable home is once beside `origin_is_same_site`
classification_rationale: DEFERRED, not fixed. Consolidating prose across two route files and repointing both call sites is a refactor of code this diff only comments on -- new surface under Test 1, not a correction. Filed rather than folded, and the irony that this is exactly the rule-in-two-places class is noted deliberately.

trigger: A reader looks for the operational rule and finds it 15 lines into a rationale block
summary: `Run it FIRST, before perm_fn` -- the load-bearing operational rule -- was pushed below the new threat-model prose
classification_rationale: DEFERRED with G1-13, since both are resolved by the same relocation.
